criteria.quote: Step on sleeping Geodude—it still won't wake.
criteria.revision: Make the condition precise while sharpening the contradiction: "Step on a deeply sleeping Geodude—and it still won't wake."

criteria.quote: A deeply sleeping Geodude buries itself halfway underground, ignores hikers stepping on it, then rolls downhill for food.
How can a buried Geodude ignore footsteps, then start moving?
criteria.revision: Make the unanswered transition more concrete: "If it won't wake when stepped on, what gets it moving by morning?"

criteria.quote: Step on sleeping Geodude—it still won't wake. / When it sleeps deeply, Geodude buries itself halfway into the ground. / Hikers may mistake it for rock and step right over.
criteria.revision: Replace the three overlapping setup beats with distinct turns: establish that deep sleep prevents it from waking, reveal that it is half-buried and mistaken for a rock, then add the researched contrast that stepping on an awake Geodude makes it angry before revealing its morning food search.

criteria.quote: Then morning arrives: Geodude rolls downhill, searching for food.
criteria.revision: Make the change in state the reveal instead of stating it as a routine transition: "The hiker gets no reaction—but by morning, that same Geodude is rolling downhill in search of food."

criteria.quote: IT DOESN'T WAKE / HALF BURIED WHILE ASLEEP / A ROCK THAT DOESN'T MOVE / STILL AT NIGHT. MOVING BY MORNING.
criteria.revision: Cut the repeated sleeping-rock captions and give each beat a different fact: deep sleep prevents waking, half-burial hides it, stepping on an awake one makes it angry, and morning sends it downhill for food.

criteria.quote: Geodude sleeps through hikers, then rolls downhill in the morning to search for food.
criteria.revision: Resolve the opening question with the researched two-state contrast: "Deep sleep keeps Geodude from waking under a hiker; morning is when it rolls downhill to search for food."

criteria.quote: Would you avoid it, or trust it to stay asleep?
criteria.revision: Make the split depend on the documented difference between sleeping and awake Geodude: "Would you step over a deeply sleeping Geodude, or avoid the trail because stepping on an awake one makes it angry?"
